images.title: Faces, edges, vertices of a prism
images.purpose: Names a face, an edge and a vertex on one triangular prism and gives the three counts.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. One large triangular prism lying like a tent in the centre, seen from the front, a little to the right and well above, so both sloping roof faces show. Three callout lines lead to three short labels at the right.
images.exact_structure: A triangular prism: front triangle and back triangle (congruent, point up) joined by 3 long edges, so 2 triangular faces and 3 rectangular faces. All 9 edges drawn dark, except the 1 hidden edge (the base of the back triangle) drawn dashed grey. The front triangular face is filled teal #0072B2 (one face picked out). The ridge, the long top edge joining the two apexes, is drawn thick amber #E69F00 (one edge picked out). All 6 corners are marked with reddish purple #CC79A7 dots. Callouts: from the teal face to '5 faces', from the amber edge to '9 edges', from one purple dot to '6 vertices'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A face is a flat surface, an edge is where two faces meet, a vertex is a corner: a triangular prism has 5, 9 and 6.
images.description: Names a face, an edge and a vertex on one triangular prism and gives the three counts.
images.context: Concept T6.C1; one image that shows only the main idea.

image_decisions.why: The three words are best learnt by pointing at one example of each on a real solid.
